steps.content:
MBCC
Chief's Office

You're enjoying a pleasant day at the Bureau. Work has wrapped up for now, and Wuhuanzi has just brought you fresh tea, the boiling tea still making wisps of steam in the teapot. Sipping the piping hot brew, you leisurely while away the final moments of your workday.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Hm? What's this...

You glance down at your tea. Emerald buds settle in a loose pile at the bottom of the cup, and among them, a single tea stem floats upright in the water. You remember hearing from a Sinner that a standing tea stem is a sign of good luck.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Good luck is welcome, of course. But honestly, I'd be perfectly content if the next few days stayed as peaceful as today.
Maybe you could leave early today, take a stroll around the grounds. Nightingale mentioned the flowers around the Bureau are in full bloom, and you haven't had a chance to see them yet...
Just as you're making up your mind, a series of panicked screams and a deafening engine roar suddenly assault your eardrums.
Instinct kicks in and you dive right. The next instant, a car smashes through a wall of the Bureau building, blasting a gaping hole into it!
Cough, cough... Oh no, oh no, they're gonna make me pay for this again, aren't they...
You're still holding that steaming cup of tea, eyes widening in shock. After a moment, a familiar mop of red hair pokes through the hole in the wall.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Hey there, Chief... Looks like we've... run into each other again.
(Transition)
Some ten minutes later, you bring this uninvited guest to the interrogation room.

To accommodate this guest with such unique abilities, Nightingale has called for an urgent reinforcement of the interrogation room and removed all sharp objects that might turn hazardous under Murphy's influence.
You silently pray that aside from that gaping hole in the wall, no further damage will be done today.
You refill your own tea and pour one for Murphy as well.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Wow, Chief, this tea stem in your cup is standing up! Could this be... the rumored sign of good luck? Does that mean I'm your lucky star today?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Good luck? All I see is the Goddess of Bad Luck I just saw off making her grand return.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Heh heh heh... Well, it's also possible that my arrival scared the tea leaves so badly they're all standing up! Pretty impressive, huh?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Hold on... hold on! I... I was just trying to lighten the mood, you know! Actually, I've just returned to my job at the Public Security Bureau's information desk. You see, I'm a perfect, law-abiding citizen!

After the previous incident, Murphy completed a simple registration and vanished. The city arrest team managed to track her down several times despite considerable difficulty, but every attempt to detain her ended in some sort of mishap. Somehow, she always slips out of the Bureau's grip.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Didn't you go home after registering with the MBCC? Why have you been wandering around again? I've been getting a ton of Mania alerts, and every single one turned out to be you.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Ahaha... Well, something went wrong with my car again... If it hadn't run out of power and fuel, I bet it would have driven itself all the way to WhiteSands!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: So after I got the car fixed, I figured, if I couldn't go back to Eastside... I could just become a delivery person or something in WhiteSands instead! Thought I could at least make a living!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I've always admired your optimism...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Then a few days later, I found out that my arrest order had apparently been retracted! So I went back to Eastside...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Though my coworkers seem to look at me a bit differently now... well, overall, my life hasn't changed that much compared to before!

The little disaster magnet is just as oblivious as ever. You let out a helpless sigh. The arrest order was retracted because you had confirmed Murphy's identity and verified that her special power posed no threat to public safety, aside from the harm she caused herself.

options: So what brought you to the Bureau today?

choices.text: So what brought you to the Bureau today?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Hmm, I just wanted to drop by and catch up with you and everyone else?
You raise your hand expressionlessly once more.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Okay, okay, I get it!
She fidgets nervously, poking her fingers together as if trying to figure out where to begin.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Okay then... Be prepared for the long story.
You nod, gesturing for her to begin.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: During those few days I was hiding around WhiteSands, I actually discovered a pattern to my bad luck!
You point in the direction of the wall Murphy just crashed through.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Hey... No, I'm serious! This time was just an accident! Let me tell you all about it...
[Insert Flashback]

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Spilled milk three times, broke my charger twice... but I won a third prize in a lucky draw! Sure, it's only a third prize... but that still counts as good luck, right?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Computer crashed three times, replaced two hard drives... but today, before it rained, I actually remembered to bring in my laundry! That's a first!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Hmm... Before, my life had been filled only with bad luck, but somehow I won a prize just a while ago?! A PRIZE! That had seriously never happened in my entire life!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Could it be...

Murphy scribbled away in her notebook. As she meticulously documented every trivial detail of her daily life, she seemed convinced she had uncovered the ultimate secret behind her luck. Even in the dim, suffocating cubicle, she became fired up with enthusiasm.
[End of Flashback]

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: So, my guess is... my natural bad luck must have evolved!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...I'm pretty sure that's just the normal everyday experience of the average person?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Rather than your bad luck evolving, I think you've simply started noticing that good things happen to you too. How long have you been experiencing this?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...Since my car sent that shadowy impostor flying last time?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...Oh! Wait, could I have... transferred all my bad luck to that thing last time? That's why my own luck seems to have improved a teeny tiny bit?
(Flashback)

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: And there's more! I've also noticed that... after a few unlucky incidents, I'll get some good luck!

options: Have you been reading too many light novels?

choices.text: Have you been reading too many light novels?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: But it's true! Chief, you have to believe me! I've been keeping track... On average, three days of bad luck will trigger a small lucky event. After a whole week of bad luck, something really good will happen!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Like... one time a car splashed dirty water all over me, then I broke a chair, and the very next day I bought the sweetest watermelon ever! Like, it was delicious! The kind that splits right open with just a tap!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: This has happened so many times! Look, I wrote it all down in my notebook!

You take the notebook Murphy hands you. The title was written with a highlighter in big letters: On the Pattern of Good Luck and the Pity System of Bad Luck. Below it, she's even carefully calculated the frequency of lucky events.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Wow, this looks like some kind of research paper... So, you seem to believe your bad luck and good luck follow a pattern, with some form of conversion and exchange going on between the two?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Like some sort of points system you see on shopping websites. Collect enough points and you can redeem a prize. Is that what you mean?
Murphy nods vigorously, her eyes brimming with hopeful anticipation as she looks to you for approval.
You consider your response carefully, and decide not to comment on her peculiar theories or her so-called pattern of good luck for now.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Alright, let's say it's true. If your luck's gotten better, then that's great, isn't it? Did you come all the way to the Bureau just to brag about it?
The corners of Murphy's mouth droop noticeably.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: No... Obviously... I came because lately, the pattern seems to behave strangely...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Two weeks ago, I got what has to be the angriest complaint call ever! This old lady was impossible to deal with. My coworkers all call her the <color=#fb9259>Cranky Old Lady</color>. She's practically become a legend at the information desk...
[Scene Change]

steps.speaker: Cranky Old Lady
steps.content: Hello?! Anyone there? Did you all kick the bucket?! I pay taxes so you people can fix those ramshackle walls, not sit around the office gathering dust!

steps.speaker: Cranky Old Lady
steps.content: How many times have I told you?! That wretched dog on the next street starts howling at three in the morning every day! Like its owner just died! Are you going to do something about it or not?! If you don't, I'll go hang myself right outside your office!

steps.speaker: Cranky Old Lady
steps.content: Say something! What, cat got your tongue?!
[Scene Transition]

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: She was basically calling every single day, complaining about late-night road construction keeping her up, or the neighbor's dog barking...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I had to listen to her rant while also helping other citizens at the information desk. The moment I was a little slow to respond, she turned on me too, calling me a lazybones who only knew how to take taxpayers' money. I remember thinking maybe I should've just called in sick that day...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: To ease the awkwardness, I asked if she wanted to grab some water and take a breather before continuing to yell at me. Next thing I knew, she just... stopped shouting and hung up.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: And then my supervisor heard the recording. He thought I showed amazing patience and handled it brilliantly. He actually held me up as the model complaint call operator and gave me a huge bonus.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Isn't that great? Sounds like you've unlocked your secret talent.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I know, right? I thought I had never been blessed with better luck too! But after that... the information desk started getting more and more complaint calls. And my supervisor would transfer all the toughest cases straight to me...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I see. So you became the complaint call specialist.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Exactly! Anyway, after that, my life changed completely all of a sudden! The little bits of good luck I was getting got rarer and smaller, and work kept getting harder.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Until yesterday... It was supposed to be a lucky day for me, but Cranky Old Lady called again! This time she was complaining about the streetlight outside her place being too bright and keeping her awake... But I'd literally just walked past that very spot the day before and tripped because it was too dark!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...If she hadn't made that call two weeks ago, I never would've gotten recognized by my supervisor or become stuck with all those awful complaint calls. If only she hadn't called that day...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: So instead of giving her my usual "Thank you for your feedback, we'll look into it," I stood my ground and firmly explained that there was absolutely nothing wrong with the streetlight's brightness.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I don't even remember what else I said, but I was so worked up. Probably went a little overboard... When I finally came to my senses, all my coworkers had stopped working and were just staring at me, and my supervisor called me into his office for a lecture...
As she speaks, Murphy's head droops lower and lower. Faint traces of Mania gather around her, forming a rain cloud above her head.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: My supervisor asked if I'd been under too much stress lately and needed some time to recharge. And that's how <color=#e88490>unlucky Murphy</color> earned herself a special day off.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I wanted to clear my head, so I went for a drive. Next thing I knew, I ended up around here. Chief, I feel like I'm slipping back to how I was before I met you. What am I supposed to do...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: You... you told me if I ever needed help, I could come to you. You meant it, right? You'll help me this time too, right?

Murphy stares at you with pleading eyes. Seeing her in such a pitiful state, you can't bring yourself to scold her any further. With a wave of your hand, you disperse the rain cloud hovering above her.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Of course. A promise is a promise.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: While I don't believe good luck appears in any predictable pattern, let's analyze the situation under the assumption that your theory is true.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Based on your records, the frequency of lucky events has dropped significantly over the past two weeks, from an average of once every three days to once every four to five days.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If we quantify the exchange rate between your bad luck and good luck, it's as if... the threshold for triggering good luck has suddenly been raised, right?
Murphy looks at you with teary eyes, as if she's just found her kindred spirit, nodding vigorously.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: You must know a way to fix this too, right? Just like how you handle Mania!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Don't look at me like that. I'm not some god of fortune. I can't just fix your "good luck probability" like that.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Normally, this theory does help you stay optimistic. But when you encounter an unlucky streak... like right now, this same theory gives you unrealistic expectations for good luck. So when things don't turn out the way you anticipate, you end up feeling even more dejected and disappointed.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're not really upset about that cranky old lady. You're frustrated because your bad luck hasn't been properly "converted" into the good luck you're expecting...
You continue taking notes while observing her expression. Then, you suddenly realize something and stop writing.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...It sounds like this theory itself is the root of the problem. Your mindset is affecting how you see things. Couldn't you abandon this theory altogether?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Actually... I don't want to. This is my hard-earned good luck, after all...
Though you remain completely unconvinced by her theory, you know such good luck is indeed hard to come by for Murphy—even if it might be nothing more than a fancy illusion.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I understand. I'll stop by your workplace later and see if I can offer some advice.
You decide to give it a shot anyway.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Hurray! I knew you wouldn't give up on me, Chief!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I thought I might lose my job because I was too frustrated, then I might lose my apartment because I couldn't pay rent, and I might end up hauling all my stuff to crash at the Bureau... Haha...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...What kind of horror story is that?

You can't help but recall what it was like when she came to the Bureau for her examinations. The constant downpours were actually the least of your problems. Glassware and ceramics were broken on a daily basis, and every so often, a few light fixtures and chunks of wall joined the casualty list.

You'd be walking around in casts every day, constantly on edge, all while enduring Nightingale's unspoken complaints and the other Sinners' resentful stares... Just thinking about it sends a shiver down your spine.
<size=44><color=#fb9259>Murphy definitely cannot move into the Bureau again!!</color></size>

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright, for the smooth operations of the Bureau, and for my own safety at work...
Have to find a way to help this Goddess of Bad Luck as soon as possible.
